purpose: Measure a bounded 1.0-degree high-speed azimuth-deadband point between the previously rejected 1.5- and 0.5-degree candidates using the normal shadow gate.

candidate.baselineFormula: azimuth_deadband_deg = 1.5 + 2.5*x; x=0 at low-speed end and 1 at high-speed end (4.0 deg)
candidate.candidateFormula: azimuth_deadband_deg = 1.5 - 0.5*x; x=0 at low-speed end and 1 at high-speed end (1.0 deg)
candidate.otherGuidanceAndLimits: Unchanged, including the low-q bank ramp, maximum bank, roll limits, AoA limits, configuration, and qualification criteria.
candidate.build: Isolated copy of the current CLanding working tree; focused entry-lateral-feedback-test passed.

interpretation.finding: The 1.0-degree point advanced the first reversal 42.8 seconds versus the 4-degree baseline and reduced closest miss from about 4.5 km to 0.6 km. Yet at 38.0 km/Mach 5.21 the shadow was already 146.4 degrees off the target course; 45 seconds later it was nearly 180 degrees off and 68.5 km away. Range error (+69.7 km) remained worse than the +64.9 km baseline and nearly identical to the 0.5-degree point (+69.6 km).
interpretation.decision: Do not adopt the deadband candidate. Stop the deadband sweep: 0.5 and 1.0 degrees give nearly the same range/course failure, while 1.5 degrees also fails MM305 and TAEM.
interpretation.limits: The gate rejected before live control or descent. This is a shadow prediction, not a flight observation or landing qualification. The low-q bank ramp, flight limits, shadow criteria, and saved checkpoint were unchanged.
